newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX sticks to bullish track, rises 0.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: German DAX sticks to bullish track, rises 0.6 pct.

text.p: A record overnight performance on Wall Street and robust dollar powered German shares to fresh heights on Thursday, as the market forged ahead with its biggest ever bull run.

Prices paused after a strong early rally, then regained steam to lift the blue chip DAX 26.07 points or 0.6 percent to a record 4,227.31 at its close. The index veered from a high of 4,272.55 to a low of 4,211.74 points during the pre-bourse and bourse sessions.

Dealers said the seesawing movement reflected a clear rise in volatility on the market, but did not imply a break in the startling uptrend which has lifted the DAX 4.6 percent this week and more than 46 percent this year.
"I wouldn't dare to go short on this market," said BHF Bank assistant vice-president of equities Josh Waiblinger.
"I might take some minor profits here or there but anything major could be suicidal."

The main early spur for the market was the surge on Wall Street which took the Dow Jones Index above 8,000 points for the first time. The dollar's firm stance at just below 1.80 marks was another key support.
Among the day's weakest performers was Volkswagen AG which dropped 30 marks to 1,445 marks amid unconfirmed talks that the carmaker had been downgraded.
Retailer Karstadt AG surged 31 marks to 694 marks, on the other hand, amid speculation that it might be taken over by Dutch supermarket group Ahold. Both companies declined comment.
Chemical stocks were also generally in demand, pushed ahead on hopes that the strong dollar and pound sterling will substantially increase their profits.
Commerzbank lifted Hoechst and Bayer to buy from hold and BASF to buy from sell, forecasting a phase of outperformance for the sector.
Bayer gained 70 pfennigs to 76.30 marks while BASF rose 30 pfennigs to 70.85 marks. Hoechst ended flat at 84.10 marks, up two pfennigs.
